title: Distributed-systems reliability
subtitle: Nothing waits on anything else, every component restarts independently, and the accounting balances.

stats.label: at-most-once windows written into the gap register
batches whose fill once blocked the broker for 17 seconds
leakage rules binding the delivery, coordination and durability planes

lede: The Inference Fabric lost work silently under load. Its buffer service is a custom distributed system: producers, a durable broker and pull-based GPU consumers on separate machines, each restartable on its own, with no distributed transactions and no shared state store on the hot path. I traced it to a definition. An item counted as consumed when it was read and was dropped if the consumer's channel happened to be full. I redefined done as delivered and acknowledged and rebuilt the accounting around it, accepting bookkeeping cost on the read path, so a full channel delays work and loses none.
quote: “Consumed on read” was the bug, and “acknowledged on completion” was the cure.
evidence: Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: a broker whose registry showed 6.67M items pending against 118K in storage, fixed by redefining done as delivered and acknowledged.
Distributed systems correctness: liveness restored after a 3,099-batch fill blocked the broker for 17 seconds, with a time budget on channel filling.
Failure-domain design: delivery, coordination and durability planes bound by 6 leakage rules, so a coordinator outage leaves delivery alone.
Delivery guarantees: 32 at-most-once windows written into a gap register instead of paying for exactly-once delivery.
author: Corey James
